Anyksciai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Utenos apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jews first came to the Anykščiai region in the 17th century; in 1704, an envoy from Hevron affiliated with the Shabtai Zvi circle — the Sabbatean movement referenced at several other sites in this collection — visited the town. The Jewish population reached 2,754 (70 percent) by 1897, and by the late 1930s the community supported six synagogues, two of them Hasidic, a yeshiva, three Tarbut schools, and an amateur theater. On June 26, 1941, the day the Germans captured the city, all Jews were forced into a synagogue and tortured, then held in a forest for weeks without shelter; between July 28 and August 29, 1941, most were murdered at nearby Liudiškiai by Germans and Lithuanian nationalists. By 1989, only 2 Jews remained.
